event_date_basis: Announcement, publication and rollout start are the same day, so there is no split to resolve. Three independent first-party confirmations: (1) both blog posts carry <meta property="article:published_time" content="2026-09-15"> and an on-page byline date 'Sep 15, 2026'; (2) blog.google's official RSS gives both posts pubDate 'Tue, 15 Sep 2026 17:00:00 +0000'; (3) the DeepMind model card is stamped 'Published 15 September 2026'. The effective date matches: Google writes 'rolling out starting today' for both models, so availability begins 2026-09-15. Caveat for the writer: 'starting today' is a start, not a completion - the rollout was still in progress as far as any source says, and the enterprise channel is a private preview. A fourth corroboration is the pricing page footer 'Last updated 2026-09-15 UTC'. slug date 20260915 and news_date 2026-09-15 are both correct.

verified_facts.fact: Google published two blog.google posts on 2026-09-15 introducing the models: the model post 'Introducing Gemini 3.8 Live and 3.8 Live Extended Thinking' and the developer post 'Build real-time voice applications with Gemini 3.8 Live and 3.5 Transcribe'. The model post's meta article:published_time is 2026-09-15 and its byline date line reads 'Sep 15, 2026'.
The developer post carries the same publication date, meta article:published_time 2026-09-15, byline date 'Sep 15, 2026'.
The model post's on-page H1 / og:title is 'Introducing Gemini 3.8 Live and 3.8 Live Extended Thinking'; the browser <title> is the shorter 'Gemini 3.8 Live & Gemini 3.8 Live Extended Thinking'.
verified_facts.verbatim_quote: Introducing Gemini 3.8 Live and 3.8 Live Extended Thinking

verified_facts.fact: The developer post's on-page H1 / og:title is 'Build real-time voice applications with Gemini 3.8 Live and 3.5 Transcribe'.
verified_facts.verbatim_quote: Build real-time voice applications with Gemini 3.8 Live and 3.5 Transcribe

verified_facts.fact: Authors of the model post are Tom Ouyang (Principal Engineer) and Malini Jaganathan (Member of Technical Staff, on behalf of the Gemini Audio Team).
verified_facts.verbatim_quote: Tom Ouyang Principal Engineer Malini Jaganathan Member of Technical Staff, on behalf of the Gemini Audio Team

verified_facts.fact: Authors of the developer post are Alisa Fortin (Product Manager, Google DeepMind) and Thor Schaeff (Member of the Technical Staff (DevX), Google DeepMind).

Two models were announced, positioned differently: 'Gemini 3.8 Live: Built for scale and cost efficiency, combining conversational intelligence with fluid dialogue and visual grounding.' and 'Gemini 3.8 Live Extended Thinking: Built for high-complexity tasks, with increased intelligence and multi-step reasoning.'
verified_facts.verbatim_quote: Gemini 3.8 Live: Built for scale and cost efficiency, combining conversational intelligence with fluid dialogue and visual grounding. Gemini 3.8 Live Extended Thinking: Built for high-complexity tasks, with increased intelligence and multi-step reasoning.

verified_facts.fact: Google frames the pair as 'our most advanced live dialogue models yet' (meta description and standfirst).
verified_facts.verbatim_quote: Gemini 3.8 Live and Gemini 3.8 Live Extended Thinking are our most advanced live dialogue models yet, built for natural conversation.

verified_facts.fact: Google says Gemini 3.8 Live processes visual inputs in near real-time, automatically detects and transitions between 97 supported languages mid-conversation, and executes tools and API calls in the background while continuing the conversation, so the model can acknowledge requests and keep chatting while tasks finish. All four capabilities named in the assignment are in this single sentence pair.
verified_facts.verbatim_quote: Gemini 3.8 Live processes visual inputs in near real-time, enriching conversations with context for more helpful responses. It automatically detects and transitions between 97 supported languages mid-conversation. It executes tools and API calls in the background while continuing the conversation, so the model can acknowledge requests and keep chatting while tasks finish in the background.

verified_facts.fact: Google says that for tasks requiring deeper reasoning, 3.8 Live Extended Thinking 'reasons and speaks simultaneously', using early verbal cues like 'Let me check that...' to acknowledge prompts, and live progress narration to walk users through multi-step background tasks as they progress.
verified_facts.verbatim_quote: For tasks that require deeper reasoning, 3.8 Live Extended Thinking reasons and speaks simultaneously. It delivers increased intelligence for complex workflows while maintaining an uninterrupted conversational flow - using early verbal cues like “Let me check that…” to acknowledge prompts naturally, and live progress narration to walk users through multi-step background tasks as they progress.

verified_facts.fact: The developer post lists five key capabilities of the pair: asynchronous function calling (execute API and tool calls in the background while continuing to stream audio responses), visual context (ground dialogue in live visual inputs), alphanumeric precision (accurately parse confirmation codes, claim numbers and technical data), multilingual support ('coverage for 97+ languages and accent consistency'), and incremental content updates.
verified_facts.verbatim_quote: Alphanumeric precision: Accurately parse confirmation codes, claim numbers, and technical data

verified_facts.fact: Google says 3.8 Live Extended Thinking supports 'configurable thinking' to handle complex, multi-step reasoning in the background while responding or narrating its progress in the main conversation, and calls the pair 'a more streamlined alternative to cascaded architectures'.
verified_facts.verbatim_quote: These models represent a step-change from our previous live models and provide a more streamlined alternative to cascaded architectures.

verified_facts.fact: The model post's video captions describe demonstrations, not measured results: Gemini 3.8 Live guiding employee onboarding using visual context, playing chess in near real-time using visual context; 3.8 Live Extended Thinking turning raw sketches plus voice feedback into functional React components, coordinating multi-step bookings and asynchronous function calls, and building business plans and marketing toolkits through speech.
Google says all audio generated by its AI products is watermarked with SynthID, an imperceptible watermark woven into the audio output.
verified_facts.verbatim_quote: All audio generated by our AI products is watermarked with SynthID. This imperceptible watermark is woven directly into the audio output, ensuring AI-generated content remains detectable to help prevent misinformation.

not_said: NO REGION OR COUNTRY SCOPE ANYWHERE. This is the single most important gap. The model post says only 'rolling out starting today' for both models and never names a country, region, market or launch order. A full-text scan of the model post, the developer post and the model card found zero region statements; the only country names on the pages are blog.google's own locale switcher in the site chrome, which is navigation, not content. The article MUST NOT imply or assume that a Taiwanese Google account can use any of this, and must say 'Google did not state the region scope'.

No interface-language scope. The 97-language figure describes what the model can detect and speak inside a conversation. Google does NOT say which interface languages the consumer surfaces (Search Live, Gemini Live, Docs/Gmail/Keep) support at launch, and does not confirm that Traditional Chinese is among the languages enabled on any consumer surface.
No date for any 'coming soon' item. Gemini Enterprise for Customer Experience, and Google Workspace business customers for Extended Thinking, are marked 'coming soon' with no timeframe.

No consumer price. The only prices Google publishes are developer API prices. Google does not state what Google AI Pro or Google AI Ultra cost, nor any usage limit, quota, session length cap or fair-use cap for consumers in Search Live, Gemini Live, Docs, Gmail or Keep.
No end date or completion date for the rollout. 'Starting today' is a start, and Google does not say when any surface finishes rolling out or how a user can tell which model they are talking to.
No eligibility detail for the enterprise private preview: no application route, no qualifying criteria, no waitlist, no participant count.
No list of the 97 languages. Google gives the count only. There is no published enumeration on any of the four sources.
No latency figures. Both posts repeatedly say 'near real-time', 'low-latency', 'impressive latency' and 'fluid', but publish no millisecond figure for time-to-first-audio or turn latency.
No independent testing. Every benchmark number comes from Google's own post citing third-party leaderboards; Mokaair has run no hands-on test, and the article must say so.

No statement on whether audio from consumer surfaces is retained, used for training, or how long it is kept. The 'used to improve our products' Yes/No split on the pricing page covers the Gemini API free and paid tiers only, not Search Live, Gemini Live or Workspace.
No accuracy or error rate for the 97-language automatic detection and mid-conversation switching, and no statement about what happens when detection is wrong.

No statement that Gemini 3.8 Live replaces or deprecates any earlier Live model. gemini-3.1-flash-live-preview is still listed on the pricing page alongside the new models, and the Live API thinking guide describes upgrading from it as optional.

No pricing distinction between Gemini 3.8 Live and 3.8 Live Extended Thinking. They share one pricing block, so the cheaper-model framing ('built for scale and cost efficiency') is about token consumption and reasoning overhead, not about a lower list price - and Google never says this in so many words.

corrections_to_candidate_list: candidates-tech-and-ai.md line 68-69 says consumers get it in 'Search Live, Gemini Live, and Workspace (Docs/Gmail/Keep) for AI Pro/Ultra subscribers'. That flattens two distinctions Google actually draws. (a) The two models have DIFFERENT consumer surfaces: 3.8 Live is 'For everyone: In Search Live' only; Gemini Live and the Workspace surfaces belong to 3.8 Live Extended Thinking. (b) The AI Pro/Ultra gate applies to Docs only - Google's words are 'for Google AI Pro and Ultra subscribers in Workspace in Docs, and all Google AI subscribers in Gmail and Keep'. Gmail and Keep are open to all Google AI subscribers, a wider group.

candidates-tech-and-ai.md line 66-67 lists 'coming soon' as Gemini Enterprise for Customer Experience and Google Workspace for both models. editorial_brief:
READER AND ANGLE. Written for a Taiwanese general reader who uses Gemini in Search, the Gemini app or Google Docs and keeps hearing that voice AI got better. The question the article answers is not 'is the model good' but 'which of these five doors is actually open to me, and what changes when I talk to it instead of typing'. The spine is the gap between a launch and an entitlement: Google shipped two models on one day into five different channels with five different conditions, and the consumer sentence is the narrowest part of the announcement, not the widest.

THE CENTRAL FACT TO GET RIGHT. Google published no region scope at all - only 'rolling out starting today'. Full-text scans of all three Google pages found no country, region or market statement. The article must say 官方未說明開放地區 plainly and must never suggest a Taiwanese account has this. This is the one thing a reviewer will check first.

THE SECOND THING TO GET RIGHT. The availability matrix is finer-grained than the candidate list records. 3.8 Live for everyone means Search Live only. 3.8 Live Extended Thinking for everyone means Gemini Live, plus Docs for Google AI Pro and Ultra subscribers, plus Gmail and Keep for all Google AI subscribers. Enterprise is a private preview for both. A table of 4 columns x 5 rows (surface / which model / who qualifies / status) carries this better than prose and is the natural fit for the BRIEF's required table at the end of section 2, caption dated 2026-09-16.

SUGGESTED FIVE SECTIONS. (1) What was announced and which model sits behind which door. (2) The four capability claims - near real-time visual input, 97-language mid-conversation switching, background tool execution without interrupting the conversation, and Extended Thinking reasoning while speaking - all attributed to Google, ending with the availability table. (3) Why 'starting today' is not 'available to you': staged rollout, private preview, subscription gates, no region statement; diagram goes here. (4) Cost and data: the free tier exists, free-tier traffic is marked 'used to improve our products', paid is not, both models share one price, per-minute figures are Google's estimate from token prices. (5) What Google did not say and what to check yourself - knowledge cutoff January 2025 despite the real-time framing, no latency figures, no language list, no consumer quota, SynthID watermarking on all generated audio.

ORIGINAL SCENARIO, to be labelled as an editorial example per BRIEF. A reader planning a trip asks Gemini by voice to compare two itineraries while showing the screen to the camera; the model acknowledges, searches in the background and narrates progress. The editorial point is not that this is magical but that three separate conditions must hold before it happens - the right surface, the right subscription, and a region Google has not named - and that a January 2025 knowledge cutoff means anything time-sensitive still depends on live search grounding, which is metered separately.

TONE AND SCOPE. Plain, specific, no hype; the article's value is the conditions, not the capabilities. Deliberately out of scope: any comparison with OpenAI's GPT-Live or any other vendor (Google makes none), any benchmark interpretation beyond reporting Google's numbers as claims, any hands-on impression, any Gemini Live productivity feature already covered on 2026-08-26, and any repeat of the 3.8 Flash cost argument from 2026-09-02.
